texts: mixed: the lighting event, both groups, the time terms and the tense all land, but "day 630 of Year 2" becomes a day-of-month term - the only day granularity the instruction set defines - and "the keepers of the East Row" falls between a possessive genitive and an agent noun's of-object, leaving the link head undetermined. For the second, a minimal edit makes it deterministic: "On day 630 of Year 2, the East Row keepers together lit the lanterns of the East Row at sundown." The day-of-year date has no licensed form at all, and "together" leaves no positive atom - the collective reading is carried only by the absence of a per-member rule; both of those are ours to fix.
good. the burning lands with the lantern group as agent, mire-essence as what is consumed, past tense, the compound decomposed, and a fireable per-member rule so each lantern's burning is derivable.

good. "Together" correctly keeps one produce event over the lantern group with no per-member distribution, and the mist-light produced is a typed individual that later sentences can refer back to. Note only that "Together" itself gets no atom - the collective reading is carried by the absence of a distribution rule.
good. the showing, the same mist-light individual as its theme, "at night" and the tense are all covered, with a fireable per-member rule over the lanterns.
good. "The mist-light" resolves to the individual the lanterns produced rather than to a bare kind symbol, and the attracted nightmoths become a group of their own.

mixed: the crowd is built correctly and "gathered" rightly stays collective on the group, but "A crowd of nightmoths" is indefinite, so it mints a second nightmoth group unconnected to the moths just attracted, and that earlier group is left with nothing further said about it. If they are the same moths, write "A crowd of the nightmoths gathered at the East Row." - the partitive "of the" makes the crowd a subset of the attracted group.
good. the four sky-cats become a counted group, both compounds get their genus atoms, the source is recorded, and the descent distributes to each cat through a fireable rule.

mixed: agent group, crowd, summer and tense are covered with a fireable per-member rule, but "at the East Row" was attached to the hunting event rather than restricting the crowd, and your sentence leaves that attachment open. If you mean the hunt took place there, front it: "At the East Row, the four sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd in summer."

bad: two losses here - "at the East Row" is dropped entirely, so the crowd's location goes unrecorded, and "shrank" is treated as though the crowd were unaffected when shrinking is exactly a change of state in it. Fronting the phrase guarantees it is kept: "At the East Row, the nightmoth crowd shrank." The role error is not caused by your wording and is ours to fix.

mixed: the survival is faithful and carries a fireable per-member rule, but nothing links the survivors to the crowd that was hunted - they are a fresh, unconnected nightmoth group. If the survivors come from that crowd, write "Some of the nightmoth crowd survived the hunt." - the partitive makes them a subset of it.
good. the flight has the survivors as agent, the Hollows as goal, past tense and a fireable per-member rule, and "the surviving nightmoths" correctly reuses the group that survived.
good. "reached the Hollows" takes the plain direct-object role, the tense is right, and a fireable per-member rule carries the arrival down to each surviving moth.
good. the molting has the cats as the ones that change, the hunt as the containing interval, and a fireable per-member rule so each cat's molt is derivable.

bad: the threads are slotted in the role for objects that are created, destroyed or changed - in both the group fact and the per-member rule - although leaving them on a lantern displaces them unchanged, so every per-member event the rule mints inherits the wrong role. Your wording does not cause this and no rewrite improves it; it is a translator-side fix. Separately, "The nightmoths" here resolves to the crowd rather than to the earlier attracted group - worth checking that is the set you meant.
